scope: One integrated export for every NASA-identified motion object in the seven audited Perpetual Ocean releases. Named eddy links and cartographic crossings are independent atlas context, not NASA model identity or feature footprints.

releases.title: Perpetual Ocean
releases.boundary_note: The southern Africa still is geographically captioned but does not name the Agulhas Current here; that name is supported by the companion 2011 story. The page mentions ocean eddies as a model-resolved class; the unannotated movie does not identify individual eddies.

releases.title: Perpetual Ocean
releases.boundary_note: The Agulhas still caption describes an eastward loop, supporting the described retroflection without using that proper name. The story's slow circular pools support an ocean-eddy class, without identifying one named pool or a bounded footprint.

releases.title: Perpetual Ocean 2: Western Boundary Currents
reviewed_parts: beauty, temperature, salinity, and deep-flow descriptions
releases.boundary_note: Cape Hatteras and Florida Straits are geographic context. The Red Sea and Persian Gulf overflow contributions are separately described flows, but NASA does not name or map their plumes. The general meander-born ring discussion is not a Gulf Stream ring identification; Gulf Stream cold cores are described separately. NASA supplies no per-ring names or dated eddy tracks on this page.

releases.title: An Ocean in Motion
releases.boundary_note: The Kuroshio Extension proper name is not used. Sinking north of the Atlantic is a described region without a NASA boundary; heat uptake and release are processes outside this motion-object ledger.

releases.title: Perpetual Ocean 2: Equirectangular
releases.boundary_note: The 70 published rectangles are video crops of the ECCO field, not 70 individually identified currents or eddies.

releases.title: Ocean Currents in equirectangular projection
releases.boundary_note: The Gulf Stream is the sole proper current name in the descriptive text; color variants do not establish separate objects.

releases.title: Perpetual Ocean 2: Polar Views
reviewed_parts: north and south polar view descriptions
releases.boundary_note: The page names viewpoints but does not identify a named current or individual eddy.

records.name: Gulf Stream
records.description: Named western boundary current in both generations; the 2011 page supplies a named still and the 2025 narration follows its North Atlantic reach. NASA's Florida Straits starting point uses a broader name scope than NOAA's strict segmented glossary.

system_context.note: NASA calls the Gulf Stream another part of the ocean conveyor belt; this is a system relation, not a streamline boundary.

releases.vertical_scope: 3D velocity field; particles seeded above and below 600 m

reported_properties.scope_note: NASA's 2011 introductory story describes the Gulf Stream and Kuroshio as examples of currents carrying warm water at speeds greater than 4 mph; no averaging interval, location, or method is supplied. This is a source-era description, not a series-wide minimum.
NASA's descriptive upper value; not a time-mean transport estimate.
NASA's Gulf Stream tour description; not a uniform temperature along the full current.

length_evidence.name: Gulf Stream
length_evidence.scope: Tomczak and Godfrey report approximately 2,500 km for the Gulf Stream proper as an open-ocean free jet downstream of Cape Hatteras toward the Newfoundland Rise/Grand Banks near 50°W. This excludes the Florida Current and North Atlantic Current; it is a textbook path-scale description, not a measured reference streamline. NOAA's glossary uses the same strict segment definition, while NASA and NOAA Coast Pilot sometimes use Gulf Stream more broadly.
length_evidence.length_source_locator: Chapter 14, The Atlantic Ocean, PDF page 11 (printed page 239), paragraph beginning Recirculation of Gulf Stream water (next 2,500 km Gulf Stream proper)

other_observations.source_locator: PDF page 3, Section 2.1 Underwater Glider Data and Methods, paragraph on 52 missions sampling a roughly 2,000 km Gulf Stream reach

records.name: Kuroshio Current
records.description: Named western boundary current east of Taiwan and Japan; the 2025 tour discusses its persistent meanders separately.

releases.vertical_scope: 3D velocity field; particles seeded above and below 600 m

reported_properties.scope_note: NASA's 2011 introductory story describes the Gulf Stream and Kuroshio as examples of currents carrying warm water at speeds greater than 4 mph; no averaging interval, location, or method is supplied. This is a source-era description, not a series-wide minimum.
NASA's Kuroshio description; no spatial or time averaging method is specified.
NASA notes seasonal variation; source gives no averaging interval or salinity unit.

reported_properties.unit: ratio to Amazon River water flow
reported_properties.scope_note: Narration cues 25–26 compare Kuroshio water flow with the Amazon River; no reference river discharge, absolute transport, averaging interval, or measurement method is supplied. This ratio is not a current length.

length_evidence.name: Kuroshio Current
length_evidence.scope: Approximate Kuroshio journey from about 12°N to 35°N in the western North Pacific; not a measured whole-current axis, and the Kuroshio Extension is separate.
length_evidence.length_source_locator: PDF page 3, Introduction opening paragraph (3,000 km journey from about 12°N to 35°N)

records.name: Agulhas Current
records.description: Named western boundary current along southeast Africa; NASA also publishes an Agulhas-specific hyperwall movie.

releases.vertical_scope: 3D velocity field; particles seeded above and below 600 m

releases.model_period_as_described: 2021–2023 in page prose; narrower metadata dates also appear

length_evidence.name: Agulhas Current
length_evidence.scope: The research description spans roughly 27°S–40°S; the coastal path is longer than its north–south separation. Retroflection, leakage, and the eastward Agulhas Return Current are distinct from this boundary-current core. The derived floor is unranked. A 2021 review also describes a roughly 1,000 km coastal segment. That narrower usage conflicts with the broader 27°S–40°S derived floor, so the two numbers are displayed as source-specific scopes and neither is ranked as a common whole-current length.
length_evidence.length_source_locator: Section The Agulhas Current, opening paragraph (27–40°S); 1,400 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

source_reported_length_variants.scope: Coastal western boundary current along southeastern Africa; narrower than the 27°S–40°S span used for the existing broad lower bound. End gates and centerline are not specified.
source_reported_length_variants.source_locator: Section 2.1.1 Background, opening paragraph (1,000 km western boundary current)

records.name: East Australian Current
records.description: Named as a western boundary current in the narrated film.

length_evidence.name: East Australian Current
length_evidence.scope: A derived minimum north–south span for the coherent shelf-break jet only; not a measured streamline or a published whole-current length. Separation and extension shift over time.
length_evidence.length_source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, opening EAC paragraph (15–32°S); 1,800 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

records.name: Indonesian Throughflow
records.description: Named interbasin flow discussed as freshwater transport from the Pacific toward the Indian Ocean.

releases.vertical_scope: 3D velocity field; particles seeded above and below 600 m

reported_properties.scope_note: NASA describes this as relatively fresh; no averaging interval or salinity unit is given.

length_evidence.name: Indonesian Throughflow
length_evidence.scope: NASA names the Pacific-to-Indian freshwater passage through narrow gaps of the Maritime Continent but gives no single current centerline or whole-system length. This is a multi-channel flow, so no length enters the ranking.

external_current_context.note: Grenier et al. identify the Mindanao Current as one feeder of the Indonesian Throughflow. NASA names the throughflow but does not identify the Mindanao Current in this release.
external_current_context.source_locator: Section 1 Introduction [4] and Figure 1 pathway description: Mindanao Current feeds the Indonesian Throughflow

records.name: Red Sea saline overflow
records.description: NASA identifies overflow input from the Red Sea as a contributor to salty western Indian Ocean water. The name and Bab el Mandeb gateway are OSW's source-backed index to that description; NASA supplies no plume boundary or path.

releases.vertical_scope: 3D velocity field; particles seeded above and below 600 m

length_evidence.name: Red Sea saline overflow
length_evidence.scope: NASA identifies a saline overflow contribution from the Red Sea to the western Indian Ocean. The gateway at Bab el Mandeb is not a measured plume endpoint or a whole-flow centerline; the downstream pathway and seasonal strength require separate observations.

records.name: Persian Gulf saline overflow
records.description: NASA identifies overflow input from the Persian Gulf as a contributor to salty western Indian Ocean water. The name and Strait of Hormuz gateway are OSW's source-backed index to that description; NASA supplies no plume boundary or path.

releases.vertical_scope: 3D velocity field; particles seeded above and below 600 m

length_evidence.name: Persian Gulf saline overflow
length_evidence.scope: NASA identifies a saline overflow contribution from the Persian Gulf to the western Indian Ocean. The Strait of Hormuz gateway is not a measured plume endpoint or a whole-flow centerline; dilution and circulation beyond the strait require separate observations.

records.name: Kuroshio eastward turn
records.description: The narrated film follows the current east from Japan across the Pacific. NASA does not call this segment the Kuroshio Extension in the narration.

records.name: Kuroshio eddies

records.description: Eastward turn south of Africa described in NASA's 2011 still caption and 2025 account; rings detach there. The name here is OSW's standard geographic label for NASA's described turn.

NASA's 2025 page describes unnamed Gulf Stream cold cores this way. Published studies describe detached Gulf Stream cold-core rings as cyclonic. NASA may mean a differently scoped feature; no individual eddy is classified here and OSW does not adopt the NASA wording as a general polarity rule.
reported_properties.review_note: The cited Gulf Stream cold-core ring study describes detached cold-core rings as cyclonic. Its ring class may not be identical to the unnamed cold cores in NASA's tour.
